parsed.explanation: The territory has documented formal protections: gender-identity anti-discrimination, a 2017 interpretation covering transgender students, marriage recognition, and repeal of the historic sodomy statute. No trans-specific border restriction, facility ban, custody practice, care denial, police targeting, or violence pattern is documented. However, entry, documents and airport screening follow unspecified federal rules, and the record contains no enforcement actions, complaints or outcomes under the local anti-discrimination law. Under combined-regime analysis, local protections are real but operationally unproven; the parent border stage is an open question, not a documented exposure. This places the territory in Reduced Risk, below anchors with documented traveller-facing border remedies and enforcement, but well above jurisdictions with criminalisation, exclusion or targeting.

entry_documents.exposure: Entry, travel documents and airport screening follow the governing state's federal rules; no trans-specific border friction or refusal is documented.
entry_documents.protection: No documented territorial border protection; the local human-rights statute does not govern federal entry screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Local protections begin after entry; border outcomes depend on unspecified federal practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented trans-specific detention, custody placement, strip-search or interrogation practice.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No specific custody protocol documented; the general human-rights statute is not shown to reach custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any detention would engage unspecified federal or territorial practices.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access restriction or birth-sex placement rule affecting visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The human-rights statute is general; no facility-specific enforcement is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities, if any, are not described in the dossier.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of care, medication confiscation or hospital-ward misplacement.
care_services.protection: Gender-identity discrimination is prohibited, but no health-specific enforcement or complaint outcome is documented.
care_services.interaction: A visitor could invoke the statute, but its operation in care settings is unproven.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence; the historic sodomy statute has been replaced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The human-rights statute prohibits gender-identity discrimination; the 2017 interpretation extends it to transgender students.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law and official interpretation are protective on paper; enforcement data are absent.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented restriction on transgender minors or school exclusion.
minors_guardians.protection: The 2017 chief legal officer interpretation applies the anti-discrimination law to transgender students.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor can point to the education protection, though no enforcement record exists.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data or documented police targeting.
street_violence_police_response.protection: General anti-discrimination law exists; no police-response or hate-crime enforcement record is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The absence of violence data is not evidence of safety; police practice is undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaints, enforcement actions or outcomes under the anti-discrimination law are documented; 2017 LGBTQ setbacks are not itemised.
remedies_unknowns.protection: The statute is operative and marriage recognition is settled, but operational remedies are unproven.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protection exists; whether a visitor could obtain timely redress is uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a visitor register, routine exclusion and no effective remedy. This dossier documents no entry bar or exclusion practice and has a protective local statute, so it is much safer.

0.55-B documents secondary screening, discretionary refusal and weak appeal outcomes. This dossier records no such border exposure and has statutory anti-discrimination protection, placing it higher, though federal border practice remains unknown.

0.75-C documents border training, a tribunal and brief-detention remedies. This dossier has broader local anti-discrimination coverage but no documented border practice or remedy outcomes, so it sits slightly lower.
0.85-A shows police training, oversight, compensation and working remedies. This dossier documents only paper protections and no enforcement outcomes, so it is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime has a protective local layer: gender-identity anti-discrimination, education coverage for trans students, marriage recognition and repeal of the sodomy statute. No documented trans-specific restriction, targeting or violence pattern appears. But the border and airport stage is governed by unspecified federal rules, and no enforcement or complaint outcome shows the local statute operating in practice. The known good is formal protection; the known gap is operational proof; the open question is federal border practice. That supports a Reduced Risk rating below anchors with documented traveller-facing remedies, but well above jurisdictions with exclusion, criminalisation or organised targeting.
